title: My New Coworker Is a Bot
summary_vi: Luyện nghe và đọc một bài bình luận về việc trí tuệ nhân tạo thay đổi công việc văn phòng, cùng các cụm từ hay dùng khi nói về công nghệ.
sentences: When my company introduced an AI assistant last spring, I was convinced it would take my job.
Instead, it took the most tedious parts of it, and I have been wrestling with mixed feelings ever since.
My name is Linh, and I manage a small marketing team in Da Nang.
Reports that once took a whole afternoon are now drafted in minutes, which has freed us up for more creative work.
Had I known how useful it would be, I would have asked for it years ago.
However, the tool is far from flawless, and its confident mistakes can slip under the radar.
Last month a client was almost sent a proposal containing statistics that the software had simply made up.
That is why every output must be double-checked by a human before it goes out.
Some colleagues worry that juniors will never learn the craft if machines do all the groundwork.
I see their point, but I think the real danger is complacency rather than the technology itself.
If we treat AI as a shortcut, we will lose our edge; as a sparring partner, we will sharpen it.
In the long run, the people who thrive will know when to trust the machine and when to overrule it.

vocabulary.example: Copying numbers from one spreadsheet to another is a tedious task.

vocabulary.meaning_vi: vật lộn với (vấn đề, cảm xúc)
vocabulary.example: She has been wrestling with the decision to change careers.

vocabulary.meaning_vi: lọt qua mà không bị chú ý
vocabulary.example: Small errors in the budget can easily slip under the radar.
He made up an excuse because he had forgotten the meeting.
Success often breeds complacency in large companies.
If we stop learning new skills, we will lose our edge in the market.

vocabulary.meaning_vi: người cùng tranh luận, đối trọng giúp mình giỏi lên
vocabulary.example: My brother is my favourite sparring partner when I rehearse debates.
Cheap tools can cost you more in the long run.

questions.question: How did the AI assistant change Linh's work?
options: It took over the boring tasks and left time for creative work
It forced her to move to another city
questions.explanation_vi: Công cụ AI đảm nhận phần việc tẻ nhạt nên cả nhóm có thêm thời gian cho việc sáng tạo.

questions.question: Why must every output be double-checked by a human?
options: The tool can state false information with confidence
Managers do not trust any technology
questions.explanation_vi: Phần mềm từng tự bịa ra số liệu mà vẫn tỏ ra rất chắc chắn.

questions.question: What does the writer see as the biggest danger?
options: Becoming complacent about relying on AI
Companies refusing to adopt new tools
questions.explanation_vi: Tác giả cho rằng mối nguy thật sự là sự chủ quan chứ không phải bản thân công nghệ.

questions.question: What can be inferred about the writer's attitude to AI?
questions.explanation_vi: Bà ghi nhận lợi ích nhưng vẫn nhấn mạnh việc kiểm tra và dùng có chừng mực.

title: The Day My Brain Pulled the Plug
summary_vi: Luyện đọc và nghe một bài tiểu luận cá nhân về kiệt sức do công việc, cùng các từ vựng nói về sức khỏe tinh thần.
sentences: Two winters ago, I stopped being able to read my own emails.
The words were there, but my brain refused to hold them, as if someone had pulled the plug.
I was a software engineer in Ho Chi Minh City, and I had been running on empty for almost a year.
At the time, I called it tiredness and told myself that a long weekend would fix everything.
It was only when my sister noticed that I had stopped laughing that I finally saw a doctor.
Burnout, she explained, is not simply being overworked; it is chronic exhaustion mixed with cynicism and falling performance.
If I had taken the early warning signs seriously, I might not have lost three months to recovery.
Part of the problem was a culture that treats exhaustion as a badge of honour.
Staying late was praised, and taking a day off was quietly seen as a lack of commitment.
Recovery meant setting firm boundaries, such as switching off notifications after seven in the evening.
It also meant asking for help, which turned out to be harder than any coding problem.
Today I still care about my work, but I no longer let it define my worth.

vocabulary.meaning_vi: ngắt, dừng hẳn (như rút phích cắm)
vocabulary.example: The investors pulled the plug on the project after two years.

vocabulary.meaning_vi: cạn kiệt năng lượng mà vẫn cố làm
vocabulary.example: By the end of exam season, most students are running on empty.
Chronic stress can weaken your immune system.
Years of broken promises had left him with a deep cynicism about politics.
Constant headaches can be one of the warning signs of overwork.

vocabulary.meaning_vi: niềm tự hào, thứ để khoe
vocabulary.example: For some people, sleeping only four hours is a badge of honour.
Parents who set firm boundaries usually raise more confident children.

questions.question: What was the first sign that something was wrong?
options: He could no longer take in the words of his emails
questions.explanation_vi: Ông không thể đọc nổi email của chính mình vì não không tiếp nhận được chữ.

questions.question: According to the writer's sister, burnout is
options: a short-term reaction to a bad week
a long-lasting state of exhaustion with other symptoms
questions.explanation_vi: Kiệt sức là sự mệt mỏi kéo dài kèm hoài nghi và hiệu suất giảm sút.

questions.question: What does the writer criticise about workplace culture?
options: It praises people who exhaust themselves
questions.explanation_vi: Văn hóa công sở coi việc kiệt sức như một huy hiệu danh dự.

questions.question: What does the final sentence suggest?
options: He has left his career for good
He now values himself beyond his job
He works longer hours than before
questions.explanation_vi: Anh vẫn quan tâm công việc nhưng không còn lấy nó làm thước đo giá trị bản thân.

title: Freedom on Two Wheels
summary_vi: Luyện nghe và đọc một bản tin chuyên đề về lao động tự do qua ứng dụng, với từ vựng về hợp đồng, thu nhập và quyền lợi.
sentences: Every morning at six, Minh Tuan switches on his phone and waits for the first delivery request to arrive.
He is one of hundreds of thousands of ride-hailing and delivery drivers working in Vietnam's big cities.
For many of them, gig work offers a flexibility that traditional jobs simply cannot match.
Drivers choose their own hours, and some earn more than they did in factories.
Yet this freedom comes at a price, since gig workers are classed as independent contractors rather than employees.
They receive no paid leave, no sick pay and, in many cases, no insurance unless they arrange it themselves.
Income can also be unpredictable, as the platforms adjust their commission rates with little warning.
"One week I make a decent living, and the next I barely break even," Minh Tuan says.
Lawmakers in several countries are now debating whether these workers deserve a new legal category.
Supporters of the gig model argue that stricter rules would drive companies out and cost jobs.
Critics reply that a business built on workers' insecurity is not sustainable in the long term.
Whatever the outcome, it is clear that the way we define work is being rewritten.

vocabulary.meaning_vi: phải trả giá, có cái giá đi kèm
vocabulary.example: Fast growth often comes at a price, usually in the form of stress.

vocabulary.meaning_vi: người làm hợp đồng độc lập
vocabulary.example: Many designers work as independent contractors for several clients.
New parents in some countries receive a year of paid leave.
The salesman earns a ten percent commission on every phone he sells.
It is hard to make a decent living as a freelance musician.
The new café hopes to break even by the end of the year.
A sustainable business model does not depend on exhausting its workers.

questions.question: What attracts many people to gig work?
options: The freedom to choose their hours
questions.explanation_vi: Tài xế được tự chọn giờ làm, điều mà công việc truyền thống khó đáp ứng.

questions.question: Why can gig workers' income be hard to predict?
options: They are paid in foreign currency
Platforms may change their commission rates suddenly
They must pay for fuel in advance
questions.explanation_vi: Các nền tảng điều chỉnh mức hoa hồng mà ít khi báo trước.

questions.question: What is the main argument of supporters of the gig model?
options: Strict rules could harm companies and reduce jobs
questions.explanation_vi: Họ cho rằng luật chặt hơn có thể khiến công ty rút đi và mất việc làm.

questions.question: What is the tone of the final sentence?
questions.explanation_vi: Câu cuối nhận định rằng khái niệm về công việc đang được viết lại, không khẳng định kết quả.

title: A Ticket to Walk Down My Own Street
summary_vi: Luyện nghe và đọc một bản tin về du lịch quá tải và ảnh hưởng đến cộng đồng địa phương, cùng các cụm từ về du lịch có trách nhiệm.
sentences: In the old quarter of Hoi An, residents now joke that they need a ticket to walk down their own street.
The town welcomed millions of visitors last year, far more than its narrow lanes were ever designed to handle.
Tourism has undoubtedly brought wealth, but it has also pushed up rents and driven out long-standing families.
Shops that once sold hardware and rice are being replaced by souvenir stalls and cafés aimed at foreigners.
The same story is told in Venice, Barcelona and Kyoto, where locals have staged protests against the crowds.
Some cities have responded by capping visitor numbers or charging an entrance fee on busy days.
Others encourage travellers to explore lesser-known districts, so that the pressure is spread more evenly.
Had authorities acted sooner, many communities might have avoided the resentment now spilling over.
Experts stress that tourists are not the enemy; it is unmanaged growth that does the damage.
Travellers can make a difference by staying in locally owned guesthouses and eating where residents eat.
They can also avoid peak season, when the strain on water and waste services is at its worst.
After all, a destination that loses its soul has little left to offer.

vocabulary.example: The new airport pushed up property prices across the region.

vocabulary.meaning_vi: bị đuổi đi, buộc phải rời
vocabulary.example: Small bakeries were driven out by the big supermarket chains.
The council is considering capping the number of tour buses downtown.
The argument was spilling over into every family dinner.
Unmanaged waste has turned the beach into a health hazard.

vocabulary.meaning_vi: tạo ra khác biệt, có tác động
vocabulary.example: Even small donations can make a difference to a village school.
Hotel rooms are twice as expensive during peak season.

questions.question: What do Hoi An residents mean by their joke about a ticket?
options: Crowds make it hard to move around their own neighbourhood
questions.explanation_vi: Đó là cách nói đùa về việc phố cổ quá đông đến mức dân địa phương khó đi lại.

questions.question: What is one negative effect of tourism mentioned?
options: Rising rents that push out long-term residents
questions.explanation_vi: Giá thuê nhà tăng khiến nhiều gia đình sống lâu năm phải rời đi.

questions.question: What do experts say about the cause of the damage?
options: Growth that is not managed properly
questions.explanation_vi: Chuyên gia nhấn mạnh thủ phạm là sự tăng trưởng không được quản lý, không phải du khách.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the sentence beginning 'Had authorities acted sooner'?
options: Tensions could have been reduced with earlier action
questions.explanation_vi: Câu điều kiện đảo ngữ ngụ ý rằng hành động sớm hơn có thể đã tránh được sự phẫn nộ.

topic: The true cost of fast fashion
title: The Five-Dollar T-Shirt
summary_vi: Luyện nghe và đọc một bài nói kiểu podcast về tác động của thời trang nhanh lên môi trường và người lao động.
sentences: Welcome back to the show.
Today I want to talk about the T-shirt you bought for the price of a coffee.
Fast fashion thrives on speed, turning catwalk trends into cheap clothes in a matter of weeks.
The industry now produces roughly twice as many garments as it did twenty years ago.
Much of that clothing is worn only a handful of times before it ends up in landfill.
A single pair of jeans can consume thousands of litres of water, while textile dyeing pollutes rivers in many countries.
Synthetic fibres such as polyester shed microplastics every time they are washed.
Meanwhile, the workers who stitch these garments are often paid wages that barely cover rent.
It would be easy to blame shoppers, but the system is designed to make buying feel effortless.
If brands were held accountable for the waste they create, prices would probably reflect the real cost.
Until then, the most sustainable garment is the one already hanging in your wardrobe.
So before you hit the buy button, ask yourself whether you will still love it in thirty wears.

vocabulary.example: Social media thrives on attention and quick reactions.
The little shop became famous in a matter of weeks.

vocabulary.meaning_vi: cuối cùng bị đổ ra bãi rác
vocabulary.example: Most plastic packaging ends up in landfill within a year.
My cat sheds hair all over the sofa in summer.
Her scholarship will barely cover her tuition, let alone living costs.

vocabulary.meaning_vi: bị buộc phải chịu trách nhiệm
vocabulary.example: Company directors should be held accountable for serious safety failures.

vocabulary.meaning_vi: bền vững, thân thiện với môi trường
vocabulary.example: Bamboo is a sustainable alternative to plastic straws.

questions.question: How does fast fashion work, according to the speaker?
options: It makes clothes designed to last decades
It copies trends and sells them cheaply within weeks
It sells only in luxury stores
It produces fewer clothes every year
questions.explanation_vi: Thời trang nhanh biến xu hướng sàn diễn thành quần áo giá rẻ chỉ trong vài tuần.

questions.question: Which environmental problem is linked to washing synthetic clothes?
questions.explanation_vi: Sợi tổng hợp như polyester thải ra vi nhựa mỗi lần giặt.

questions.question: What does the speaker say about blaming shoppers?
options: It is easy, but the system is built to encourage buying
Shoppers have no choice at all
questions.explanation_vi: Người nói cho rằng hệ thống được thiết kế để việc mua sắm trở nên dễ dàng nên không chỉ đổ lỗi cho người mua.

questions.question: What is the speaker's final advice?
options: Think about long-term use before buying
Give old clothes to the factory
questions.explanation_vi: Người nói khuyên tự hỏi liệu mình còn thích món đồ sau ba mươi lần mặc hay không.

title: Pause, Rewind, Repeat
summary_vi: Luyện nghe và đọc một bài bình luận so sánh học trực tuyến với học trên lớp, cùng các liên từ nối ý quan trọng.
sentences: When classes moved online in 2020, I assumed it would be a temporary inconvenience.
Five years on, I am a university lecturer in Hanoi who teaches half of her courses through a screen.
Online learning has undeniably widened access, allowing a farmer's daughter in Gia Lai to attend lectures from top universities.
It also lets students learn at their own pace, pausing and replaying a difficult explanation as often as they need.
Yet I have noticed that motivation tends to evaporate without the structure of a physical timetable.
Completion rates for free courses are strikingly low, often falling below ten percent.
In a classroom, a confused face is noticed immediately, whereas on a video call it is easily hidden behind a muted camera.
Casual conversations in corridors, which shape friendships and ideas, are almost impossible to replicate online.
That said, I would not want to go back to a purely traditional model.
The best results come from blended learning, where lectures are watched at home and class time goes on discussion.
Whichever format is chosen, success depends less on the technology than on the quality of the teaching.
A mediocre lecture does not become inspiring simply because it is streamed.

vocabulary.meaning_vi: mở rộng khả năng tiếp cận
vocabulary.example: Public libraries have widened access to books for poor families.

vocabulary.meaning_vi: theo tốc độ của riêng mình
vocabulary.example: Children should be allowed to read at their own pace.
My enthusiasm began to evaporate after the third rainy day.
Completion rates rise when courses include short quizzes.
No app can replicate the atmosphere of a live concert.

vocabulary.meaning_vi: học kết hợp (trực tuyến và trực tiếp)
vocabulary.example: Our school adopted blended learning to make better use of class time.
The film was too long; that said, the ending was brilliant.

questions.question: What is one advantage of online learning mentioned?
options: It is always cheaper than school
It lets students from remote areas attend top lectures
It removes the need for teachers
questions.explanation_vi: Học trực tuyến giúp cả những học sinh ở vùng xa tham dự bài giảng của trường hàng đầu.

questions.question: Why does the writer say a confused student is harder to spot online?
options: Cameras and microphones can be switched off
questions.explanation_vi: Sinh viên có thể tắt camera hoặc micro nên khó nhận ra vẻ bối rối.

questions.question: What does the writer prefer?
options: A mix of home lectures and in-class discussion
questions.explanation_vi: Tác giả thấy kết quả tốt nhất đến từ mô hình học kết hợp.

questions.question: What is the point of the last sentence?
questions.explanation_vi: Bài giảng tệ không thể trở nên hay chỉ vì được phát trực tuyến.

title: The Cinema in My Pocket
summary_vi: Luyện nghe và đọc một bài tiểu luận cá nhân về việc các nền tảng phát trực tuyến thay đổi ngành điện ảnh và thói quen xem phim.
sentences: As a teenager, I once queued for two hours to see a film that had already been out abroad for months.
Today the same film would be waiting on my phone before I finished my breakfast.
Streaming platforms have turned the entertainment industry upside down in barely fifteen years.
Studios that once relied on box office takings now compete for monthly subscriptions.
As a result, thousands of hours of content are made every year, and audiences are spoilt for choice.
This has opened doors for stories from outside Hollywood, such as Korean dramas and Spanish thrillers that found global fans overnight.
Directors enjoy bigger budgets and more creative freedom than they would have been given by a traditional studio.
On the other hand, the sheer volume makes it hard for quieter films to get noticed.
Shows are cancelled after one season if the algorithm decides they are not worth the gamble.
Cinemas have suffered too, although the best ones have survived by offering an experience that a sofa cannot match.
Personally, I binge-watch more than I would like to admit, and I rarely remember what I have seen.
Perhaps the real luxury today is not having more choice, but having the patience to choose well.

vocabulary.example: The pandemic turned our travel plans upside down.
The sequel was a huge success at the box office.
In this street food market, you are spoilt for choice.

vocabulary.meaning_vi: chỉ sau một đêm, rất nhanh
vocabulary.example: The young singer became famous overnight after one video.
The writer accepted the job because she was given complete creative freedom.
The sheer volume of emails made it impossible to reply to everyone.
Opening a restaurant in a quiet town seemed worth the gamble.

questions.question: What contrast does the writer open with?
options: Waiting for films used to take much longer
questions.explanation_vi: Trước đây phải xếp hàng và chờ hàng tháng, nay phim có sẵn ngay trên điện thoại.

questions.question: What benefit of streaming is described?
options: Stories from outside Hollywood can reach a global audience
questions.explanation_vi: Phim Hàn và phim Tây Ban Nha tìm được khán giả toàn cầu nhờ các nền tảng.

questions.question: Why might quieter films struggle on streaming platforms?
options: There is so much content that they are overlooked
They are too expensive to make
questions.explanation_vi: Khối lượng nội dung khổng lồ khiến phim nhỏ khó được chú ý.

questions.question: What is the writer's attitude in the final sentence?
questions.explanation_vi: Tác giả suy ngẫm rằng điều quý giá là biết chọn lọc chứ không phải có thêm lựa chọn.

title: Sleep Is Not Wasted Time
summary_vi: Luyện nghe và đọc một bản tin khoa học về tầm quan trọng của giấc ngủ, cùng từ vựng về sức khỏe và thói quen sinh hoạt.
sentences: Sleep used to be treated as wasted time, something ambitious people could cut down to make room for success.
Research over the past two decades has overturned that belief.
During deep sleep, the brain clears away waste products and moves the day's memories into long-term storage.
Adults who regularly get less than six hours are more likely to develop heart disease and depression.
Even a single bad night can dull attention, much like drinking a couple of glasses of wine.
Teenagers are especially vulnerable, since their body clocks naturally shift later, yet school often starts at dawn.
Several districts that delayed the first bell by an hour reported better grades and fewer car accidents.
Dr Ana Ferreira, a sleep researcher in Lisbon, says people routinely underestimate how impaired they are.
"If you need an alarm and a coffee to function, you are probably carrying a sleep debt," she explains.
Simple habits help: a consistent bedtime, a cool dark room and no screens for an hour beforehand.
None of this is glamorous, but it works better than any supplement on the market.
In short, a good night's sleep is not a luxury; it is the foundation on which everything else is built.

vocabulary.example: The doctor told him to cut down on salt and sugar.
The new evidence overturned the court's earlier decision.
Elderly people are more vulnerable to extreme heat.
Flying across time zones confuses our body clocks for days.
Never underestimate the power of a good night's rest.
A weekend lie-in cannot repay months of sleep debt.
The plan was costly and slow; in short, it was a mistake.

questions.question: What did research over the last two decades show?
options: Sleep can be shortened without harm
Sleep is essential, not wasted time
questions.explanation_vi: Nghiên cứu đã bác bỏ quan niệm coi giấc ngủ là thời gian lãng phí.

questions.question: What happens in the brain during deep sleep?
options: It stores memories and clears waste
questions.explanation_vi: Trong giấc ngủ sâu, não dọn chất thải và đưa ký ức vào kho lưu trữ dài hạn.

questions.question: Why are teenagers especially at risk?
options: Their body clocks shift later but school starts early
questions.explanation_vi: Đồng hồ sinh học của thiếu niên lệch muộn trong khi giờ học bắt đầu rất sớm.

questions.question: What does Dr Ferreira imply about people who rely on alarms and coffee?
options: They probably do not get enough sleep
questions.explanation_vi: Cô cho rằng cần báo thức và cà phê để tỉnh táo là dấu hiệu đang nợ giấc ngủ.
